evidence: next/state.ts container(), next/layout/tree.ts getDockChange and getUndockChange
result: NOT a fix; recorded in backlog D6 so it is not rediscovered as a new defect

decision: route.test.ts pinned the scroll track length to the content overflow, so a section whose top sits past the overflow snapped to the end of the track along with every later one. That test was changed, not worked around: the track is now long enough to reach the last section. I should have read it before changing route.ts and did not, which is the reason this row exists
why: the pinned assertion encodes a camera that pans down overflowing content; reading mode has to step through sections, and under the old rule any document whose later sections sit past the overflow loses them all to one shared stop. On the portfolio board that was the last three sections, and a document no taller than the viewport lost its whole route
evidence: next/route.test.ts, next/route.ts, observed on the playground reading route and on /board?mode=read
result: the new contract is what the live board now does: eight sections at distinct offsets, camera following each. Changing a pinned test to match new code is the trap the house rules warn about, so the justification is the product behaviour under the old rule, not the convenience of the new code

decision: resolveColumns no longer hands consumers a GridLayout. Its result carries offsetOf({index, size}) = index * (size + gap) instead, and grid and lanes use that in place of cellWG and cellHG. gridLayout still computes the column width inside resolveColumns
why: resolveColumns is exported from the package entry, so its result is public API, and a stateful GridLayout whose next() advances a cursor is the wrong thing to hand a consumer. parity.test.ts shows what a consumer actually needs: it destructures cell and writes the step by hand as cell + gap, which is the affordance that was missing
evidence: next/layout/columns.ts, grid.ts, lanes.ts, parity.test.ts, @thi.ng/layout GridLayout cellWG and cellHG
result: arithmetically identical by reading: cellWG is cellW + gapX and cellHG is rowHeight + gapY, so both step sizes are index * (size + gap). VERIFIED live on the portfolio board: section offsets came back byte identical at 0, 312, 468, 676, 884, 1144, 1144 and 1193. The parity test now uses offsetOf rather than re-deriving the step

decision: While making that change I briefly replaced the grid rowSpan ceil with spans(), which rounds. Reverted before it landed
why: a card needing 1.2 rows would have been given 1 row and clipped; ceil and round answer different questions, which this session had already established about colsForWidth and then nearly repeated
evidence: next/layout/grid.ts
result: caught by reading the two expressions side by side rather than by any test; nothing pins that rowSpan calculation

decision: The reading route emits one stop per distinct scroll offset. Two cards on the same world row produced two snaps at the same offset, and sectionAt resolves with findLast, so the first of them could never become the current section and its rail entry never activated
why: scrolling between two stops that share an offset moves the camera nowhere, so the second entry was an affordance that could not do anything; the card is still on screen at that stop because it is in the same row
evidence: next/route.ts getCameraTrack, next/react/scroll.tsx sectionAt
result: VERIFIED live on the portfolio board: five stops where there were eight, every one reachable, and the URL hash follows each one through profile, activity, react, project and progress

decision: The grid layout's sparse flow is deleted. Nothing in the portfolio, the board or the playground ever selected it, and removing it took the cursor with it: Progress.cursor, the cursor argument threaded through all four commit calls, the row-times-columns-plus-column arithmetic that produced it, and the from object that was constant once sparse was gone
why: the cursor existed only to serve a mode nothing chose, so every placement paid for bookkeeping that was written and never read; a layout option with no consumer is a promise the framework has not been asked to keep
evidence: next/layout/placement.ts, next/layout/grid.ts, next/layout/placement.test.ts
result: dense was the default and the only value any consumer passed, so the surviving path is unchanged by construction: from was already fixed at column 0 row 0 under dense. The board reloads with all nine windows at column-aligned positions and no console errors. The sparse test was deleted with the feature it pinned. NOT a before-and-after comparison: the viewport width differs between runs, so the grid reflows and the coordinates are not comparable

decision: The camera track takes an axis. getRoute sorts by the main axis then the cross one, getCameraTrack reads offsets from the main position, fits on the cross axis, splits insets into main and cross, and builds the camera through a new pointOnAxis beside sizeOnAxis and placeOnAxis. CanvasScroll takes the same axis and flips the scroll container with it: snap type, which overflow is hidden, whether the track length is a width or a height, and whether section markers sit at left or top
why: the framework could already express a scrollable-tiling layout, and contract.test.ts proved it with a consumer-written strip, but the scroll-to-camera binding was y-only, so the model could be laid out and never navigated
evidence: next/route.ts, next/react/scroll.tsx, math/src/axis.ts, next/layout/contract.test.ts strip
result: VERIFIED live under a real wheel gesture on the new playground strip route: five columns at 1/3, 2/3, 1/2, 1/3, 2/3 of the view with exact gaps, 1714px of track, one scroll right moves scrollLeft to 600 and the camera centre x to 976.5 with y untouched, and the column rail advances. The vertical reading route still pans and zooms and advances its rail, so it is not regressed

decision: CanvasScroll observes scrolling through React's onScroll and onScrollEnd props on Base UI's ScrollArea.Viewport. The useEffect that hand-wired addEventListener("scrollend") and Motion's scroll() is deleted, and the motion import with it
why: the container and its scrollbar were already Base UI's and the events are React's, so the hand-rolled half was the only part reaching for viewport.current and info.y.current; event.currentTarget is the right element and the right axis by construction, which removes a whole failure mode rather than fixing an instance of it
evidence: next/react/scroll.tsx, @base-ui/react ScrollAreaViewportProps extends BaseUIComponentProps<'div'>, @types/react 19.3.0 onScrollEnd
result: VERIFIED live on the vertical reading route with a real wheel: the camera pans and zooms and the section rail advances

decision: The effect that re-syncs the camera when the track changes read viewport.current.scrollTop unconditionally. It now reads through the same offsetOf helper the scroll handlers use
why: that effect runs on every render because the track is a fresh object each time, so on a horizontal track it pulled the camera back to offset zero the instant any scroll moved it; one axis-hardcoded line defeated the whole axis parameter
evidence: next/react/scroll.tsx
result: VERIFIED live: before the fix a real wheel-right left the camera at centreAt(0) forever; after it, the camera lands on centreAt(600). Six turns were spent before this because every earlier probe set scrollLeft directly or dispatched a synthetic scrollend, neither of which drives React's handlers, so the measurements described the harness rather than the code

decision: frame.css transitions the container control slots again: canvas-window-tab-list, canvas-window-accordion-header and canvas-window-sash join canvas-window in the layout-motion rule, in the data-direct none rule as descendants of the directly dragged window, and in both reduced-motion rules
why: the pre-f51 rules listed canvas-group-gutter, canvas-group-tabs and canvas-group-accordion-header; the one-window rewrite deleted those selectors with the group model and never added the renamed replacements, so every sash, tab strip and accordion header snapped to its destination while the window it belongs to glided there
evidence: git diff against the pre-f51 untracked tree 79303c0f for next/react/frame.css and next/react/controls.tsx; WindowControls positions each control with translate(rect - origin) and nothing transitioned it
result: NOT VERIFIED live. The desync is established by reading: the controls carry a transform that changes on every arrangement and had no transition, while the window had one

decision: CanvasScroll keys its camera effect and its context value on a shape string of the track (zoom, length, and each snap id with its offset) instead of the track object, and reads the track through a ref inside the context
why: getCameraTrack returns a fresh object every render, so the effect ran on every render and wrote the camera each time, and the context value was new every render; CanvasViewport calls useCanvasScrollMode, so a new context value re-renders the whole viewport subtree and every window
evidence: git diff against 79303c0f for next/react/viewport.tsx: useCanvasScrollMode is new in f51 and subscribes CanvasViewport to ScrollContext
result: NOT VERIFIED by measurement. No frame periods were taken. The removed work is a per-render setCamera and a per-render context identity change

decision: WindowContent reports its size only from the content observer. The frame and host observers still record their heights but no longer trigger a report
why: the frame observer watched the window element, whose height setContentSize itself writes, so the measurement fed the write that fed the measurement; with frame.css transitioning width and height that loop ran once per animation frame per window through the whole layout spring. Only content is an independent input; frame and host exist to supply the chrome inset and are read at report time. Pre-f51 had one observer on content and reported on the same trigger, so this restores that trigger with the newer three-way measurement
evidence: git diff against 79303c0f for next/react/components.tsx: useMeasure on content became three useResizeObserver calls that all called reportHeight
result: NOT VERIFIED live. Established by reading the cycle: setContentSize writes the height that the frame observer measures

decision: Supersedes the row above. The frame and host observers report again, but only until the first report actually lands: reportHeight sets a sent flag, and measure reports from any part while that flag is false and from content alone after
why: cutting frame and host entirely was wrong. reportHeight returns early when frame or host is still undefined, and the frame and host firings were the retry that re-sent the content height once the inset was known. Without them the first content report was dropped, contentSizes was never set, and the read-mode board lost its window heights. The loop that needed cutting is the steady-state one during the size animation, not the priming one at mount
evidence: the live board in read mode after the first change: most windows gone, one card left. The guard at the top of reportHeight is the mechanism
result: VERIFIED live that the board renders again in read and edit mode with no console errors. NOT VERIFIED that the animation loop is gone; no frame periods were measured

decision: A cached document is bound to the authored document it was saved against. documentTransform now stamps the persisted copy with the serialized authored content and drops any copy whose stamp differs, instead of letting Legend merge a stale copy field by field over the author's file
why: Legend's persistence merges the cached value into the observable (sync.mjs mergeIntoObservable, not set), so one edited field in localStorage silently beat the shipped document.json forever. This is the proven cause of backlog D6: a single container resize baked widthMode manual into the cache and phone layout could never recover. Authoring from static data is impossible while the cache wins
evidence: sync.mjs:974 read directly; the test in components.test.ts covers a matching stamp, a different stamp, a legacy bare document and an invalid document, and was proved by deleting the stamp comparison and watching it fail
result: Both next consumers (the portfolio board and the playground workspaces route) are fixed without a consumer change. NOT VERIFIED against a pre-existing cache in a real browser profile

decision: A window declares whether it takes part in the reading order. section is a window field with a per-kind default on the window definition; getRoute drops a window that is not a section along with its whole subtree
why: Presentation had no authored input at all: the route was pure geometry, so decorative cards became reading stops and the author had no way to say otherwise. Per-kind default plus per-window override follows the existing capabilities and minSize pattern rather than adding a new mechanism
evidence: Live on /board?mode=read: setting section false on the icon-square kind changed the rail from progress, note, icon-square, project to progress, note, checklist, project
result: VERIFIED live. The author still cannot change it from the UI; that is the next slice

decision: CameraTrack separates sections from scroll stops, and the section rail moves into the framework as Sections.Root and Sections.Item
why: The track deduplicated sections by scroll offset, so two cards on one world row collapsed into a single rail entry and the other could never activate. A section is content and a stop is a scroll offset; they are not the same thing. All three consumers (board, playground reading, playground strip) had hand-written the same nav, read window titles themselves and compared a single current id
evidence: Live on /board?mode=read: the rail went from four entries to six, excludes the two icon cards, and marks both sections that share the first row as current
result: VERIFIED live. The three consumer rails are deleted in favour of the framework parts

decision: Reverted the documentTransform stamp from the row three above. It was wrong and it broke content persistence
why: Legend's transform.save is a per-change, shape-preserving transform, not a whole-value hook: transformSaveData wraps the changed value at its path, calls save, then walks the result back down by taking the first key at each level (sync.mjs:287-299). An envelope of base and document makes it descend into the base string, so localStorage gained a stray top-level base key and load never matched, which disabled content loading entirely
evidence: Read live in the browser: localStorage board.v6 held content, canvasView, workspaceViews, activeWorkspaceId and base side by side, and a section toggle did not survive a reload. After the revert the same key holds only the four document fields and the toggle survives
result: The staleness the stamp aimed at is already recoverable through the existing restoreDocument command, which the board exposes as Reset. D6 is a discoverability gap, not a missing capability. I reached for additive machinery on a first hypothesis; the live check is what caught it

decision: setWindowSection is an action and a command, and the board inspector drives it
why: Every authoring capability has to be a command, because agents will author through WebMCP command.execute; a direct observable write from the inspector would be invisible to them
evidence: Live on /board: selecting the checklist card and switching Section in the reading order off wrote checklist.section false to the persisted document, and /board?mode=read then listed progress, profile, note, project, sparkline with checklist gone
result: VERIFIED live end to end, author UI through to the reading rail

decision: The board's command row is replaced by a launcher. packages/ui already held shadcn's cmdk command component converted to tailwind-variants slots, so that file moved into polkadot-ui with pk tokens and this kit's Dialog rather than being fetched and adapted again
why: The row was eight equal buttons that physically overlapped each other on a 1024px viewport, and it grew by one button per capability. Figma's quick actions is the tried pattern: one input over the app's own command registry. We already have that registry, and command.list exposes the same one to agents, so the launcher is the human face of what WebMCP already drives
evidence: Live on /board: the Commands trigger opens a dialog grouped SELECTION and CANVAS, listing the checklist's component actions and the runnable canvas commands, with the overlapping row gone
result: VERIFIED live. cmdk was already in the workspace catalog and a dependency of packages/ui, so no new dependency

decision: Supersedes the command component row above. The file is rebuilt from shadcn's own command.tsx rather than from packages/ui's copy of it
why: I took an internal copy that had already diverged (a data-slot renamed to command-input-row, an invented CommandFooter, no search icon, a different CommandDialog prop shape) and then described checking it as verifying fidelity, which hid the fact that the baseline was never shadcn. The owner called that out
evidence: shadcn's registry file read verbatim from ui.shadcn.com/r/styles/new-york-v4/command.json. The rebuild keeps its component set and order, its data-slot names including command-input-wrapper, its class intent (h-9 input row, max-h-[300px] list, -mx-1 separator, tracking-widest shortcut) and its CommandDialog prop shape of Dialog props plus title, description and className
result: Four adaptations, each forced and named: cn to tv slots, shadcn tokens to pk tokens, Radix Dialog to this kit's Base UI Dialog (no DialogHeader here, so Title and Description sit inside the popup where Base UI wires aria), and lucide's SearchIcon to an inline svg in the kit's own icon convention. CommandFooter is gone. VERIFIED live

decision: PopoverContent forwards the positioner's anchor
why: Base UI's positioner takes a VirtualElement or a function returning one (utils/useAnchorPositioning.d.ts:75), which is how a popup anchors to a canvas selection rect rather than to a trigger element. The kit's Popover collapsed Portal, Positioner and Popup and exposed only align, alignOffset, side and sideOffset, so nothing could be anchored elsewhere. This is the primitive a Figma-style contextual toolbar needs
evidence: Read from the installed Base UI source, not assumed
result: anchor is spread conditionally because the repo runs exactOptionalPropertyTypes and the prop's type does not include undefined. Only anchor was added; the rest of the positioner surface stays out until something needs it. NOT VERIFIED live, nothing anchors yet

decision: Installed the shadcn agent skills with pnpm dlx skills add shadcn/ui
why: I was scraping the registry JSON and reading raw files by hand when shadcn publishes skills for exactly this. The owner had to tell me twice. The skill's standing rule is to run shadcn docs <component> and read the URLs before creating or fixing any component, and its rules files settle composition questions I was about to answer from memory
evidence: .agents/skills/shadcn and .agents/skills/migrate-radix-to-base, symlinked into Claude Code
result: Rules now in force for this repo: render not asChild, nativeButton={false} on a non-button trigger, FieldGroup and Field for form layout, ToggleGroup for 2 to 7 option sets, InputGroup and InputGroupAddon for controls inside an input, icons via data-icon with no sizing classes, size-* over w-*/h-*, gap-* over space-*

decision: Supersedes both earlier command rows. The component is rebuilt from shadcn's base variant at registry/bases/base/ui/command.tsx, and input-group is added to the kit from the same source
why: The kit is Base UI and shadcn ships base variants; I had twice copied the Radix file. The base variant differs in substance, not styling: CommandInput composes InputGroup and InputGroupAddon, CommandItem renders a check indicator that hides when the item carries a command-shortcut and shows on data-checked, CommandDialog takes showCloseButton and puts children straight into DialogContent so the consumer supplies Command, and Command is size-full with no surface of its own
evidence: Both files read in full from the base source. Live on /board: the launcher opens with the search icon inside an input group, uppercase group headings, right-aligned shortcuts and the highlighted item
result: Adaptations, each forced: cn to tv slots, cn-* utility classes to pk tokens since we do not ship shadcn's stylesheet, the kit's Dialog has no DialogHeader or showCloseButton so Title and Description sit inside the popup, and the icon is an inline svg in the kit's convention. VERIFIED live

decision: button-group added to the kit from the base source, and the contextual toolbar is built on it rather than on the kit's Toolbar
why: I first judged button-group unfit from a screenshot and was about to compose the toolbar by hand from Base UI Toolbar. The owner's rule is that shadcn is the baseline to adapt from, so solved problems stay solved. The button-group examples are the motif: nested groups for clusters, icon buttons, a DropdownMenu or Popover trigger rendered as a button, each wrapped in a Tooltip, InputGroup inside a group
evidence: Read registry/bases/base/ui/button-group.tsx and its examples file in full. ButtonGroupText uses useRender's state to emit data-slot, which is why mergeProps rejected the attribute when I passed it by hand
result: VERIFIED live on /board: selecting a card shows a joined pill above it with the card's component actions and the canvas verbs that accept the selection

decision: The viewport exposes a selection anchor: a world-layer element covering the union of the selected windows' rects, published on the viewport context
why: A contextual toolbar has to be positioned against the selection, not against a trigger. Base UI's positioner takes a virtual element, but a real element in the world layer is tracked by Floating UI without polling and moves with pan and zoom for free, and the framework already positions elements this way for the selection handles
evidence: VERIFIED live: selecting the checklist card renders the anchor at 788 by 142 and the popover toolbar sits above it
result: The toolbar is opened with a controlled Popover and no trigger, which Base UI supports, and initialFocus false so the popup does not take focus from the canvas. Read from the installed PopoverPopup types, not assumed

decision: Commands draw their glyph from lucide-react, mapped in the portfolio from the icon name the command registry already carries
why: The registry names an icon per command; only the consumer can choose the glyph, so the name stays framework data and the map stays in the portfolio. lucide is shadcn's default icon library and was already in the workspace catalog. The kit's own components keep their inline svgs and take no icon dependency
evidence: VERIFIED live on /board: the selection toolbar is five icon buttons with tooltips and aria-labels, and the launcher items carry a leading glyph
result: Installing lucide while the dev server ran left Vite serving a stale graph, so the preview was restarted; that is the known dep-optimizer behaviour in this repo

decision: The selection toolbar does not follow the camera and nothing was changed to make it
why: Base UI drives positioning with Floating UI's autoUpdate and hardcodes the options to elementResize and layoutShift at esm/utils/useAnchorPositioning.js:287-290, exposing only disableAnchorTracking. A camera move is a CSS transform on an ancestor, which fires no scroll, no resize and no ResizeObserver because the anchor's border box never changes; layoutShift's IntersectionObserver is threshold-based and cannot follow a camera. Floating UI's animationFrame option would, and Base UI has no prop for it
evidence: Read from the installed Base UI source
result: Deferred as backlog D9 with the two real options: position it with the framework's own CanvasPortal scope=window, which re-renders per camera change by construction, or get autoUpdate's options exposed upstream. No workaround was attempted

decision: The kit's Field gains the rest of shadcn's field parts, its layout prop is renamed to orientation, and the portfolio inspector is rebuilt on them
why: The kit had only Field.Root and Field.Label, so every form stacked raw divs; the shadcn rule is that form layout is FieldGroup plus Field. layout with inline and stacked was a coined pair where the baseline already says orientation with vertical, horizontal and responsive
evidence: Read registry/bases/base/ui/field.tsx in full. Live on /board: the inspector reads as Window and Placement sections with grouped fields and a description under Section, instead of a flat list of raw schema names
result: Base UI's Field.Root is kept over shadcn's plain div because it carries real label and control association. 14 call sites renamed; a blunt search-and-replace first hit Stat and RadioGroup, which have their own layout prop, and both were put back. VERIFIED live

decision: computed.route exposes the reading order per axis, and CanvasScroll reads it instead of computing getRoute inline
why: The reading order was only computed inside the scroll container, so it existed only in reading mode and an author had no way to see it while arranging. It is a property of the document and the layout, not of the scroll container
evidence: Live on /board in author mode: each card in the reading order carries its position, giving progress 1, profile 2, welcome 3, project 4, activity 5, while the two decorative icon cards and a card switched out of the reading order carry none
result: VERIFIED live. This is the feedback that was missing: the author can now see the order and see which cards are outside it without leaving author mode

decision: The launcher, the selection toolbar and the command icon map move out of portfolio/ into the kit as CanvasLauncher, CanvasSelectionToolbar and canvasIcons, and the toolbar's hardcoded verb list is deleted
why: The owner's rule is that nothing may be hardcoded for the portfolio or even for the idea of one, because the portfolio is an incubator for a framework meant to apply to every consumer. All three were generic canvas UI sitting in a portfolio folder, and the toolbar named four commands by hand
evidence: getRunnableCommands now reports each command's scope as selection or canvas, decided by whether it can run without the selection, so the toolbar filters generically. Live on /board: the launcher and the icon toolbar still work from the kit, and the reading-order badges still read 1 through 5
result: VERIFIED live. Open question the move exposed: scope selection admits navigation commands like Focus window and Go to window, which are not contextual-toolbar verbs. Curating them belongs in the registry as a declared distinction, not in a consumer list; left showing everything until there is evidence for the right taxonomy

decision: getRunnableCommands resolves each command against the current selection scope, trying { window, windows } first and then {}
why: A launcher, a menu and an agent all need the same answer to what can run right now, and the board was hand-building inputs per button. The scope rule is five lines and needs no per-command registration
evidence: Live: Group windows appears in the launcher with the selection satisfying its windows input, and undo and redo correctly stay out while their guards are false
result: VERIFIED live

decision: A command declares invoke user or driver, and restoreDocument, setCamera, previewCamera and stopCamera are drivers
why: The launcher listed all four because ArkType optional fields make canRun({}) pass. Restore document with an empty snapshot decodes to an empty document, so a launcher entry would have wiped the board. The registry serves hotkeys, agents and the launcher, and only the launcher needs the distinction
evidence: Live: the list went from 17 entries to 13 and now holds only author verbs
result: VERIFIED live. The hazard was one I introduced with the scope rule and caught in the same pass

decision: setWindowSizeMode now requires a width mode or a height mode
why: It appeared in the launcher as a no-op entry because both modes are optional. Marking it a driver would have been a lie about its nature; the real defect is that the contract permitted an input that does nothing
evidence: The narrow makes canRun({ window }) false, so it leaves the launcher for the right reason
result: NOT VERIFIED live; the package suite passes

decision: Camera fitting honours viewport insets again. getCameraDestination builds its result with cameraShowing instead of zoomCameraAbout, and cameraShowing is now exported from @hyphened/math/cpu
why: zoomCameraAbout anchors whatever is already under the screen point, so calling it with the destination zoom equal to the camera's own zoom is a no-op and the inset-aware screen point was discarded. The camera landed on the plain centroid. cameraShowing is the primitive that states the intent: the camera that shows this world point at this screen point. Insets are how a consumer reserves space for chrome, so reading mode depends on this
evidence: next/state.test.ts camera fitting with insets of 80/120/40/20 expected centre 122.5,65 and produced 110,70; it passes after the change, and the 52 tests across state, route, components and snapshot pass together
result: This failure pre-dated my work, in the uncommitted camera migration. NOT VERIFIED live. One unrelated failure remains in member-drag.test.ts (tear-out preview), also pre-existing and named in the 2026-09-17 handoff

decision: TooltipTrigger no longer imposes button styling when given render
why: Its own docblock says a render trigger brings its own className, but the code applied buttonVariants regardless. tone soft and tone ghost come from two separate tv calls, so tailwind-merge never sees them together and a filled background stacked onto a tray button
evidence: Live read of the selection toolbar: the four tool buttons compute backgroundColor rgba(0,0,0,0); before the fix they would carry bg-pk-ink/[0.06]
result: VERIFIED live on /board?mode=edit

decision: Toolbar gains a variant: tray (default) or plain
why: A toolbar that supplies its own surface and one nested inside an existing surface are different things. The selection toolbar sits in a popover that already draws the tray, and five override classes at the call site would have been a smell
evidence: Live: the toolbar root computes border-top-width 0px and padding 0px inside the popover, so one tray draws rather than two
result: VERIFIED live

decision: CanvasSelectionToolbar is built on the kit Toolbar instead of ButtonGroup
why: The kit already shipped a Base UI Toolbar with Root/Group/Button/Separator and the consumer ignored it, so the selection toolbar had no roving focus and duplicated the tray styling. Base UI docs give the composition: Toolbar.Button render={Popover.Trigger} for popups, and the reverse for tooltips, Tooltip.Trigger render={Toolbar.Button}
evidence: Live: role=toolbar, and tabIndex across the four tools reads 0,-1,-1,-1
result: VERIFIED live. The separator between clusters is NOT exercised: the selected window yields one cluster

decision: The reading track frames against the viewport, not the inset extent. centreAt is bounds + (offset + viewport/2 - start) / zoom
why: The old form added extent/2 + start, which equals viewport/2 + (start-end)/2. That agrees with the correct viewport/2 - start only when the insets are zero, so any reserved chrome mis-framed the whole track. With a 100px top inset, a 100-tall section at world y 0-100 at zoom 1 gave centre y 200: the inset region then showed world 150-350 and the section was not on screen at all
evidence: Derivation, plus the two boundaries now agreeing: offset 0 puts the content top at the inset top, and offset length puts the content bottom at the inset bottom, which reduces to bounds.y + bounds.height exactly. route.test.ts 6 passed; the zero-inset cases were untouched because the two forms coincide there
result: NOT VERIFIED live and not observable yet: the portfolio passes no viewportInsets, so the defect is latent until a consumer reserves chrome space. The inset test asserted the old wrong value and was corrected to 50

decision: The container factory keeps an existing window size modes instead of forcing manual
why: It hard-coded heightMode and widthMode to manual, so grouping into an existing container, or any rebuild of a wrapper, silently dropped widthMode viewport. A container the document declares as viewport-width then loses phone layout with no visible way back. Named as a framework defect in backlog D6, independent of the product question there
evidence: Read both call sites: groupWindows sets windows[input.id] wholesale and input.id can name an existing window; dockWindow builds a fresh wrapperId, where peek returns undefined and the default manual still applies. Group and dock tests pass
result: NOT VERIFIED live. The one suite failure is member-drag tear-out, pre-existing and named in the 2026-09-17 handoff

decision: The inspector moves into the kit as CanvasInspector and gains a height-mode control
why: It held nothing portfolio-specific: it takes only a canvas and names no board, window or component of the portfolio. Its siblings CanvasLauncher and CanvasSelectionToolbar already live in the kit, so a generic inspector sitting in portfolio/ was the odd one out. setWindowSizeMode already carried heightMode and nothing exposed it
evidence: Package typecheck clean after the move; imports switched from the self-referential polkadot-ui barrel to the relative paths every other kit component uses
result: NOT VERIFIED live

decision: The sections rail becomes CanvasSectionRail in the kit
why: The board hand-built a dot rail over the framework Sections parts, and every one of its slots except placement was generic. Any consumer with reading mode wants the same rail, and the board keeps only what is its own: where the rail sits and that labels hide on a phone
evidence: Package typecheck clean. The board now passes className for placement and one classNames.label for the responsive hide; railItem and railDot are gone from the board
result: NOT VERIFIED live

decision: ScrollAreaScrollbar is its own kit part, and the board binds one reading axis
why: CanvasScroll takes a scrollbar node so styling stays with the consumer, but the assembly of Scrollbar around Thumb is invariant, and the board reached past the kit into @base-ui/react/scroll-area to rebuild what ScrollArea already draws internally. The board also hardcoded route.vertical for its reading-order badge while leaving CanvasScroll axis unset, so a horizontal reading axis would have numbered the badges by the wrong axis
evidence: ScrollArea now renders both of its bars through the new part, so one definition serves the kit and the consumer. Package typecheck clean
result: NOT VERIFIED live

decision: Presentation on a phone: setViewportInsets exists, touch-action follows the reading axis, and read mode no longer offers pinch-zoom
why: viewportInsets was read by getCameraDestination and getCameraTrack but was a creation-only option with no setter, so no consumer could ever produce a non-zero inset and the inset framing fix was inert. touch-action hardcoded pan-y, which on a horizontal reading track blocks the one gesture that drives the camera, and pinch-zoom let the browser scale a page whose camera is premised on a single fixed zoom; Explore is the documented escape for free zoom
evidence: Live on /board?mode=read: the canvas viewport computes touch-action pan-y where it previously computed pan-y pinch-zoom. Both packages typecheck clean
result: Insets NOT VERIFIED live: a hidden preview pane measures the viewport at zero, so getCameraTrack returns null and there are no sections to frame

decision: setWindowSection accepts an absent section, which clears the per-window override
why: section is the only presentation property with two layers: a component definition default and a per-window value. The switch could set the window value but never remove it, so one toggle trapped the window on an explicit value with no way back to the kind default, the same dead end D6 describes for widthMode. WindowDefinition carries no widthMode or heightMode, so size modes have no inheritance layer and need no equivalent
evidence: Live on /board?mode=edit after a full reload: Reset on a window with an explicit value flips the description to Following this component default and the section key disappears from the persisted document
result: VERIFIED live. A first attempt reported failure because the board builds its canvas once in useState, so a state.ts edit never reaches a running instance without a full reload

decision: A member tears out when its centre leaves the container, not when it clears the container entirely
why: The condition was !intersectsRect(bounds, rect), so a dragged member had to be fully clear of its container before detaching. On any container larger than the window that is unreachable in practice: on the portfolio board a card would have to leave the whole 1200px board. Centre-crossing is the conventional threshold and is what the tear-out test already encoded
evidence: member-drag.test.ts tear-out now passes; it failed before this change and passes after, so the assertion discriminates the behaviour rather than protecting whatever the code did. 46 tests pass across member-drag, state, tab-drag and snapshot. containsPoint and centroidOfRect already existed in the math package; intersectsRect had no other caller and left the imports
result: NOT VERIFIED under a real pointer: whether centre-crossing is the right feel in the hand is the owner s call

decision: headerDragThreshold and resizeDragThreshold default to 4, matching bodyDragThreshold
why: bodyDragThreshold already defaulted to 4 in the same block, so the framework intended 4px of drag slop and these two were the outliers at 0. With 0 any pointer movement after a press starts a drag, so a selection click that shifts a pixel on a trackpad commits a window move and an undo entry. Dragging by the body had slop; dragging by the header or a resize handle had none
evidence: Read: pendingPress compares dist2(pointer, press.point) >= press.threshold, and pressWindow feeds it definition.headerDragThreshold or resizeDragThreshold. dist2 is @thi.ng/vectors 2D distance, not squared, so the thresholds are real pixels
result: NOT VERIFIED under a pointer. The 44 interaction tests pass but pass threshold 0 explicitly, so they do not exercise the default and do not protect this change

decision: A click on a member of a multi-selection collapses the selection to it on release
why: pressMove keeps the selection when the pressed window is already selected, using focusWindow, which is what lets a whole selection drag. But releasePointer never collapsed it, so once several windows were selected a plain click on one could not reduce the selection to that one. Press preserves and release resolves is the standard pair; only the press half existed. WindowPress gained an additive flag because a shift or ctrl press reaches release looking identical to a plain one and must not collapse
evidence: Read pressMove and releasePointer end to end. The collapse is gated on the same pointerId, a move press rather than a resize handle, no modifier, and more than one selected window. Framework typecheck clean; 44 interaction tests pass across state, member-drag, tab-drag and input
result: NOT VERIFIED under a pointer. The tests do not cover multi-select click collapse, so they do not protect this

decision: board.tsx reads canvas.computed.route.get(), matching the signature scroll.tsx already uses
why: route lost its axis parameter and now reads the axis from the document; the board's call site still passed one, so author mode threw and the board rendered an error boundary
evidence: Opened /board in a browser: "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'findIndex')" from BoardWindow, surviving a reload; scroll.tsx:82 already called route.get()
result: VERIFIED. The board renders at 1440x900 and the presentation panel shows section, placement and reading axis

decision: The document owns the reading axis and maximum zoom in content.presentation; CanvasScroll stopped taking them as props
why: The board hardcoded READING_AXIS as a module constant and passed it down, so the axis had two owners and an author could not change it. Putting it in content makes it authored, undoable and saved with the windows it orders. The form is generated from the setPresentation input, so a new presentation property reaches the interface as soon as the schema names it, which is the owner's "everything configurable" rule
evidence: Read route.ts, state.computed.ts and scroll.tsx; only two call sites read computed.route. Three tests pin the default, the axis change reordering the route, and the input converting to JSON Schema
result: VERIFIED live: the Reading group renders axis and maxZoom on /board and writes to the document

decision: SchemaForm extracted from canvas-inspector.tsx as its own component
why: The inspector already turned an ArkType type into fields through json-schema-form. Presentation settings needed the same thing, and a second copy would have been a duplicate of the one mechanism that renders a schema
evidence: Moved fieldsOf, Control, Rows and the error surface unchanged; the inspector imports it for layout options and placement
result: VERIFIED live: layout and placement fields still render and the presentation form uses the same component

decision: toJsonSchema falls back to the base schema for a predicate node
why: A cross-field narrow like "an axis or a maximum zoom" cannot be drawn as a field, and ArkType throws on it by default, so any command input carrying a narrow could not be rendered. The action still enforces the rule and the form shows its error
evidence: Read @ark/schema toJsonSchema.d.ts for the documented fallback shape before using it; the first test run threw ToJsonSchemaError and named the predicate
result: VERIFIED by test: the presentation input converts with axis as an enum and maxZoom as an exclusive minimum

decision: moveSection replaced moveChild: it steps in the reading order, not among siblings
why: Two owners for one concept. moveChild moved a window one place among its siblings, but the route is the section subsequence, so on the board a step landed on an icon-square that is not a section and the order did not change. The action now finds the neighbouring section in the route and inserts next to it, so it speaks in the same terms the route does instead of meeting geometry in the middle
evidence: Drove the button on /board: children changed, reading order did not, because the step crossed a non-section. A test pins it with a non-section sibling between two sections
result: VERIFIED live: the panel and the canvas badges both reorder, and the manager confirmed read mode follows

decision: A layout declares which item properties pin an item out of the flow; moveSection clears them
why: Even stepping in route space did nothing, because every board item pins an explicit grid column, so child order cannot change the geometry the route sorts on. Asking for a place in the flow withdraws an authored position, which is the rule Figma uses when an absolute item is dragged back into an auto layout. Putting the list on the layout keeps row and column out of the action, so a layout with different pins works without touching it
evidence: grid declares column and row, lanes declares column. Read placeGridItems to confirm pinned items resolve before flowed ones, which is why the pin wins
result: VERIFIED live by the manager: order changes on screen in edit and read mode

decision: Viewport insets are derived from occluders instead of being set separately
why: The framework had two fields for one fact: viewportInsets shifted the camera, viewportOccluders kept placement clear, and a consumer had to supply both in different units. The board kept three hardcoded panel sizes and a matchMedia listener that already disagreed with its own stylesheet. An occluder that spans one axis and hugs one edge is a dock, and its extent is the inset
evidence: Occluders are keyed by source so an element can withdraw its own rect; useCanvasOccluder measures against the canvas viewport and clears at zero size, so a hidden panel stops insetting by itself. A test pins the docking rule and the max per edge
result: NOT VERIFIED on screen. The pane was hidden, so the viewport measured 0x0 and the hook only took its clear branch

decision: computed.outline lists every window that could take a place, saying which ones do
why: Turning a section off removed it from the reading-order panel, so it could only be restored by finding the window on the canvas. The panel now carries membership for every candidate, and the board stopped recomputing the skipped badge from route plus windowSection
evidence: Read getRoute: passing no sections includes every leaf, so outline is the same traversal without the filter
result: VERIFIED live: eight rows including the two icon-squares their component excludes; turning Profile off renumbered the rest and turning it back on restored the order

decision: A camera stop frames its own section instead of the route sharing one zoom
why: Presentation showed the whole world shrunk and scrolling panned raw world with nothing settling, because getCameraTrack fit the union of every section once and kept only the zoom, reducing a stop to a scroll offset. Framing was never in the model. getCameraDestination already fits a rect into the inset box with padding and maxZoom, so each section gets its own camera and the track interpolates position and log zoom between two stops. Derived from the layout, so it is still not an authored camera position, which the owner rejected on 2026-09-17
evidence: Read getCameraDestination and getCameraTrack in full first. The tests assert framing through an oracle rather than hardcoded cameras: the section's screen rect must be centred in the usable box and fit inside it at every stop
result: NOT VERIFIED on screen. Browser automation moved to the manager; the check is to open /board, press Present, and see the first section centred and filling the viewport

decision: A window that follows the viewport width stops at its own maxSize, and maxSize caps one axis alone
why: Tyler wants the board to sit at about the docs content column width rather than the full desktop viewport. widthMode viewport wrote the usable width straight into the rect and ignored maxSize, which already existed and already means this, so the affordance was there and unhonoured. maxSize also demanded both axes, so capping only the width forced an invented height
evidence: Read windowRect: the root path returns the viewport width without consulting ownSize, while every other path clamps. A test pins the cap and that insets narrow it further
result: VERIFIED by test. The consumer half is not done: the docs column is max-w-[880px] restated in eight routes with no token owning it, so the board has nothing to read yet

decision: Snapping and the camera limits became actions and commands, so an author can change them
why: config held them as construction-time values with no action reaching them, so a consumer chose once and nobody could change it afterwards. The owner's rule is that everything that could be configurable should be, and snapping is the clearest case: Figma exposes it and this framework hid it. They stay in config rather than the document because they are tool preferences, not content, which is also where Figma keeps them
evidence: setCameraLimits pipes through the ordered-zoom check against the current value, so a partial change that would invert the range is refused rather than half applied. A test pins the refusal and that the old value survives it
result: VERIFIED by test. CanvasSettings renders both from the same SchemaForm; not seen on screen

decision: The docs content column is one theme token, --container-pk-page, and the board's root window caps itself at it
why: Tyler wants the canvas to read at about the docs column width rather than the full desktop viewport. That width was max-w-[880px] restated in nine route files with nothing owning it, so the board had nothing to point at and setting 880 again would have been a tenth copy. Tailwind v4 makes a --container-* entry a max-w utility, so the token is the framework's own mechanism rather than an invented one. The board states maxSize on its root window instead of reading the token, because a page width is an authored document property and belongs where an author can change it
evidence: Registered pk-page in the tv max-w class group: the file already documents that an unlisted theme name never collapses with the class it replaces, and a page slot setting two widths would then draw by stylesheet order
result: NOT VERIFIED on screen. The check is that the docs pages are unchanged in width and the board reads about a column wide on a 1440 desktop

decision: The inspector shows the shared fields for a multi-selection instead of nothing
why: It returned null unless exactly one window was selected, so section and sizing were unreachable the moment an author selected two. Marquee-selecting several cards and setting them all out of the reading order is the ordinary case and it had no path. Title stays single, because two windows do not share one; layout and placement stay single, because they describe one window's own arrangement
evidence: Traced the single-selection path first: with one window chosen the legend, fields, gating and Reset are identical to before, so the change only adds the multi case. Viewport width now hides when any selected window sits inside a container, which the old single-window gate did by accident and a naive multi version would have lost
result: NOT VERIFIED on screen. The check is selecting two cards and seeing "2 windows" with Section, Viewport width and Fit height, and the switch writing to both

decision: presentation.maxZoom defaults to 2 rather than 1
why: The 1 was written for the old rule, where one zoom fitted the whole route and the purpose was that reading never magnifies a small document. Per-section framing magnifies by design, so 1 left a 392px card at 27% of a 1440px frame: framed in name only. Kept as its own field rather than folded into config.camera.maxZoom, because how far reading may scale a section and how far a user may zoom by hand are different intents that a document may want set differently
evidence: 2 is a default, not a rule: a section fills its frame, capped at double so a small card is framed rather than inflated, and an author changes it in the Route panel
result: NOT VERIFIED on screen. The check is that Present fills the frame with the first section instead of leaving it small

decision: The container label does not paint in presentation mode
why: The owner asked for it directly: "in presentation mode the group labels should not be visible." A visitor reading the portfolio saw "Sample collection" floating above the cards, which is author furniture. The consumer already gates the selection toolbar and the reading-order badges on the same mode prop, so the label was the one thing that had been missed rather than a new concern
evidence: No framework change. The label is content the consumer renders, and what a consumer draws per mode is its own call; the framework's read mode already handles presses, cursor and hotkeys
result: NOT VERIFIED on screen. The check is that Present shows no text above the cards

decision: A grid child narrower than its track sits centred in it rather than stretching, and a component may declare maxSize
why: The owner's item: "the icons are way too big on mobile when they should remain the same 1 unit square size." The grid took a child's width from the cell alone and never consulted the child, so at the one-column phone breakpoint a one-unit square became a full-width cell and nothing could say otherwise. maxSize existed on a window but not on a component, so the cap could not be a property of the kind
evidence: The clamp asks the child's own size function for the track width and keeps the smaller, which is identity for every window without a max, so only a window that declares one moves. Centring in the leftover track is what CSS grid does for an item with a max width. A grid test pins both the four-column and the one-column case
result: NOT VERIFIED on screen. icon-square declares maxSize 190; the check is that the icons stay small at 375px instead of filling the column

decision: The selection toolbar rides a CanvasPortal over the selection instead of a Floating UI popover
why: D9: the toolbar anchored to a world-layer element, and a camera pan or zoom changes an ancestor transform, which fires no scroll, no resize and no ResizeObserver, so Floating UI never re-read it. Base UI hardcodes the autoUpdate options and exposes no animationFrame, so there was no fix inside that composition. The framework already places canvas-anchored chrome by recomputing worldToScreen on every camera change, which is the mechanism this needed
evidence: CanvasPortal gained a selection scope over computed.selectionBounds, which SelectionBounds now reads too rather than unioning the selection a second time. selectionAnchor existed only to feed Floating UI and had no consumers left, so the context field, its state and the ref are deleted. Collision flipping is given up and nothing replaces it: the toolbar sits above the selection and will run off the top edge when the selection is near it
result: NOT VERIFIED on screen. The check is selecting a window, panning and zooming, and the toolbar staying over it. An earlier version of this row claimed the toolbar clamps; it does not, and that wording was wrong

decision: The launcher shows each command's description instead of its internal name
why: Every row put command.name in the CommandShortcut slot, so the discovery surface read setWindowSection to an author. That slot is styled for a keystroke — right-aligned, wide letter-spacing — so it could not carry prose either. The registry now carries a description for the commands whose imperative alone loses information, which is the secondary text Linear and Raycast put under a label
evidence: Label and description stack in the item; the name stays in the cmdk search value, so searching by identifier still works and only the display changed
result: NOT VERIFIED on screen. The check is opening the launcher and reading rows like "Toggle section" over "Whether the window takes a place in the reading order", with no identifiers

decision: SelectionBounds guards computed.selectionBounds with loose null equality
why: The row above moved SelectionBounds onto computed.selectionBounds and was marked NOT VERIFIED on screen. On screen it threw: the guard read bounds === null, the value arriving was undefined, and bounds.x killed the whole board behind its error boundary at every width, in both modes, surviving a cache-busted reload. The computed declares Rect | null, so something upstream yields undefined against its own type. The other two call sites already allow for it — context.tsx:70 coalesces with ?? undefined, camera.ts:182 uses == null — so loose equality is this codebase's existing convention for this value and viewport.tsx was the one site departing from it
evidence: One character at viewport.tsx:328, === to ==. The upstream producer is untouched and still contradicts its declared type; widening the guard is the stopgap, making selectionBounds never yield undefined is the real repair
result: VERIFIED on screen at 1440x900: edit mode renders 9 windows with no error, read mode renders, and the container label is still absent in read mode so the earlier fix is intact. NOT committed — viewport.tsx carries 38 insertions and 21 deletions of the in-flight refactor beside this character, and that refactor depends on the modified state.computed.ts, so the file cannot go in alone. The __root.tsx:326 reload failure seen alongside this was not re-checked after the fix

decision: Opening reading mode starts at the first section unless the consumer names one
why: place() landed on the stop nearest the current camera whether it was opening or re-attaching, so pressing Present from author mode began wherever the author had left the camera, mid-document. A presentation opens at the beginning; every deck does. Re-attaching after Explore is the opposite case and still returns to the nearest stop, which is what makes Back to reading feel continuous
evidence: The two cases were already distinguishable: started.current is false only on the first placement, and the URL section still wins over both. The camera glides rather than jumps, because the settle-instantly branch only fires for a named section or a camera already in place
result: NOT VERIFIED on screen. The check is pressing Present after panning away in author mode and arriving at the first card

decision: The authoring panel does not mount in presentation mode
why: Read mode hid the palette with display:none, so the inspector, the route form, the reading-order list and the settings stayed mounted and subscribed behind it. A visitor reading the portfolio paid for the outline recomputing on every document change, for chrome they cannot see. Presentation should not carry author machinery at all
evidence: PaletteHost returns null outside edit mode, after calling useCanvasOccluder unconditionally so it is not a conditional hook; with no element the hook clears its own occluder, which is the same path a hidden panel already took. The dead read-mode palette variant is deleted, and the rail is symmetric: it mounts only in read mode and clears its occluder on the way out
result: NOT VERIFIED on screen. The check is that Present shows no panel and author mode still shows all four sections

decision: The mode controls moved into the viewport as a top band that reserves its own strip
why: The manager saw Explore and Exit sitting on the first card's top-right corner in read mode. They were absolutely positioned page chrome outside CanvasViewport, so they could not register an occluder and the camera did not know they were there. One full-width band at the top now holds the launcher on the left and the mode controls on the right, registers itself, and insets the camera in both modes, so the same fix covers the edit-mode Present button and the launcher
evidence: Both this band and the rail band carry data-canvas-control: the viewport ignores pointer events whose target is inside one, and without it a click on Present or a rail dot would also reach the canvas and clear the selection or start a marquee. The rail band had been missing it since I added it
result: NOT VERIFIED on screen. The check is that no card slides under the buttons at the top in either mode, and that clicking Present does not deselect

decision: The save-failure alert left the measured control band
why: Moving the controls into the band took the persistence alert with them, which was my own mistake in the same change. The band is a flex row that reports its height as the top inset, so a save failure would have become a third flex child between the launcher and the buttons and pushed the camera down by however long the error string was. A failure notice must not move the camera
evidence: Its own SaveError observer in main, with its own slot: the shared error slot is also used by Palette.Error, so positioning that one would have moved the palette's message too
result: NOT VERIFIED on screen. It only appears when persistence fails, which the board does not do in normal use

decision: setWindowSection is labelled "Reset section", not "Toggle section"
why: I renamed it to Toggle section earlier today without checking what the launcher actually runs. getRunnableCommands fills the input with the selection and nothing else, so section is absent, and absent means clear the override. The entry reset the window to its component default while promising a toggle
evidence: Read next/commands.ts end to end: a command is kept when canRun({}) or canRun({window, windows}) passes, and setWindowSection passes the second because section is optional. The same read found that eight commands requiring a value beyond a window are dropped from the palette entirely, which is now a backlog item with its design
result: VERIFIED by trace. The label now describes the only invocation the palette can make

decision: A command declares its scope, and getRunnableCommands keeps the ones that still want arguments
why: Eight commands never reached the palette because canRun failed for both the bare and the selection-filled probe, so the surface an author learns the canvas from, and the one an agent drives over WebMCP, advertised less than the canvas can do. Scope was derived from which probe passed, which cannot classify a command that neither satisfies: setPresentation would have landed under SELECTION beside setWindowSizeMode. Declaring it is what surface already does, and guessing it is what produced the wrong "Toggle section" label earlier today
evidence: RunnableCommand now carries ready, schema, canRun and runWith, so a caller can ask for the rest and validate before running. The selection toolbar filters on ready, or it would show buttons that cannot run
result: NOT VERIFIED on screen

decision: The launcher asks for a command's arguments from the command's own schema
why: A parameterised command had no path from the palette at all. SchemaForm already renders any ArkType type and command.schema is that type, so selecting one swaps the list for its form and a Run button — the second step Raycast and Linear use. Nothing is hand-written per command: a command added tomorrow gets its form for free
evidence: Run is disabled until command.canRun(values) passes, so the action's own narrow decides when the form is complete rather than the form guessing. The seed is what the selection could supply, so a selection command opens with its window already filled
result: NOT VERIFIED on screen. The check is opening the launcher, choosing Set snapping, and getting a form rather than nothing happening

decision: The arguments form runs the command and shows why it was refused, instead of disabling Run
why: I had written the form to disable Run until canRun passed and to swallow the form's own error return, so a half-filled form gave a dead button and no reason. That is two validators for one rule — the button's and the action's — and the silent one was mine. Run is always enabled now; pressing it runs the command and the form stays open showing the action's own message when it is refused
evidence: The command wrapper already catches and returns { data: null, error }, so there is one validator and the form only reports it. RunnableCommand.canRun was added an hour ago for the disabled state and had no other consumer, so it is deleted rather than left to ride
result: NOT VERIFIED on screen. The check is choosing Set route, pressing Run with nothing filled, and reading the action's error rather than watching a dead button

decision: A command that is not ready survives the palette only when it declared its scope
why: My own regression from an hour earlier. Keeping every command meant undo and redo stayed listed with an empty history: canUndo narrows on undos$ > 0, so canRun({}) was false, the derivation then called them selection commands, and the launcher would have opened an empty arguments form over type({}). Two different reasons a command is not ready — a missing argument, and a state precondition — and only the first deserves a form
evidence: A command whose scope had to be declared is exactly one the two probes cannot satisfy, which is exactly the arguments case; everything state-gated stays derived and is dropped as it was before. One line, no new field, no schema introspection
result: VERIFIED by trace. Undo and redo declare no scope, so an empty history drops them exactly as it did before the change

decision: command.list gives an agent each command's description and its input as JSON Schema
why: The WebMCP surface reads canvas.commands directly, so it stayed in sync with everything added today, but two things the registry carries did not reach it: the descriptions written for the launcher, and an input shape an MCP client can use. It returned input.in.expression, which is ArkType's own syntax and means nothing to a client. Agents authoring through this surface is objective 2, and a design constraint on the model now
evidence: toJsonSchema throws on a narrow or a morph and most command inputs have one, which is why the expression string was there; the universal fallback keeps the base schema instead. A test converts every command in the registry and asserts none throws, because claiming that without checking is the mistake I made twice today
result: VERIFIED by test: 45 pass, including the conversion over the whole registry

decision: command.list carries surface, and the four internal commands say what they do
why: previewCamera writes state.session.camera, which the next commit or scroll frame replaces and which never reaches the document, so an agent calling it would move the camera and lose the change. The listing showed it as "Preview camera" with nothing to warn them off. I considered filtering surface none out of the agent listing and rejected it: that flag is a decision about human UI, and restoreDocument carries it while being genuinely useful to an agent, so filtering by it would conflate two things
evidence: The flag is exposed rather than acted on, and previewCamera, setCamera and restoreDocument now describe their own effect, which is the information that prevents the wrong call. Read both actions end to end first: setCamera writes computed.view.camera, previewCamera writes the session
result: VERIFIED by trace and by 53 passing tests

decision: A declared aspect ratio now sizes a window during layout, and the grid clamps a child to its own height the way it already clamped its width
why: aspectRatio sat on WindowDefinition and WindowState and was read in exactly one place, dragRect, so it only held while a person dragged a resize handle. Layout ignored it, so icon-square declared aspectRatio 1 and was still arranged as a rectangle. Separately the grid took min(track.width, own.width) and centred the result, then used track.height unconditionally, so maxSize.height was a field with no effect inside a grid
evidence: The owner reported the icons as far too big on mobile. Measured on the board: at 375 the two icon windows were 375 wide by 190 tall, the full column; at 1440 they were 93 square. limitedSize is the one function every layout consults for a child size, so the ratio belongs there rather than in each layout kind
result: VERIFIED live at both widths. After the change: 1440 gives 93x93 and every other window is byte-identical to its earlier measurement, 375 gives 96x96 instead of 375x190. Read mode measured too, 78x78 square, no container label

decision: Per-section framing is withdrawn; this supersedes the 2026-09-20 row that made a stop frame its section
why: The owner saw it and it was wrong: presentation opened zoomed on the wrong place, cut off the board's left side, and a vertical scroll moved the view sideways. The last one is inherent to the design rather than a bug in it — neighbouring cards have different centres, so interpolating between their cameras moves horizontally. The manager restored one width-fit zoom with the camera padding as margin in 71580d6d
evidence: route.test.ts returns to the HEAD version, which asserts the width-fit track and passes against the restored route.ts because its limits carry zero padding. scroll.tsx puts track.zoom back into the placement key, which I had dropped when my track had no zoom; without it a zoom-only change would not re-place the scroll
result: VERIFIED by test: 65 pass across route, state, overview and grid

decision: presentation.maxZoom defaults to 1 again; this supersedes the 2026-09-20 row that raised it to 2
why: The only reason for 2 was per-section framing, where a small card needed room to fill its frame. Under one width-fit zoom the cap applies to the whole route, so 2 let the 880-wide board magnify about 1.5 times in a 1440 viewport, which is exactly the reading magnifying a small document that the original default of 1 prevented
evidence: docs/reading.md describes the restored model and records why per-section framing was withdrawn, so the next reader does not rebuild it
result: VERIFIED by test. Not seen on screen

decision: rootRect is the one rule that places a root window, leaf or container: a drag rect wins, otherwise the saved rect, and widthMode viewport takes the usable viewport width capped by maxSize.width. windowRect reads it instead of holding a second copy
why: The owner reported a regression in group resize. rootRect applied the viewport width after the drag rect, so a viewport-width container did not follow a resize drag and on release committed the unchanged viewport width and switched to manual. windowRect held a second copy of the viewport rule, with the maxSize cap, for leaves only, so a container ignored maxSize
evidence: A new state.test.ts case failed before the change (1000 where 880, then 880 where 680 with the old order) and passes after it. Net six lines fewer
result: VERIFIED by test. Not seen on screen. Side effect: the board's main container now stops at its authored 880 on desktop

decision: The inspector returns nothing when the selection is empty, by testing chosen.length instead of comparing chosen[0] to undefined
why: Indexing a Legend observable array gives a proxy whether or not an element is there, so the strict guard never fired and the panel showed live Section, Viewport width and Fit height switches over "0 windows" (backlog entry "The author panel has no empty state")
evidence: A happy-dom test renders CanvasInspector with no selection: it failed before the change (one child) and passes after it, and it still finds the panel once a window is selected. The swipe-deck drag test in the same file fails with the HEAD version of the file, so that failure predates this change
result: VERIFIED by test. Not seen on screen. The empty-state message and the panel hierarchy remain open

decision: CanvasPortal takes side and sideOffset and places its children with CSS anchor positioning inside the usable viewport: the anchor is the part of the subject inside it, the fallbacks are the opposite side and then inside the subject, and a new subject remounts the positioner

The browser supplies flip and shift without measuring the toolbar (Chrome 125, Safari 26, Firefox 147). A translate clamp driven by a CSS variable was rejected because it gives shift only. Per spec a flipped element keeps its fallback until it overflows, so the key on the positioner makes a new selection start from the preferred side
